subject: ventures/therapy-8-minute-rule-calculator
professional: an outpatient PT/OT billing and compliance specialist (CPC with therapy-audit experience), working from the CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Pub. 100-04, ch. 5, section 20.2 (Rev. 11129) and its 8-minute-rule examples

evidence.correctness: Downloaded the CMS manual itself (cms.gov clm104c05.pdf returned 200 through the proxy; pdftotext, section 20.2 C) and wrote an independent checker (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/091d6275-30d5-5492-8889-4ef9ed0beb80/scratchpad/therapy-8-minute-rule-calculator/cms.mjs). The unit table matches the manual's ranges for every whole minute 0..300 (0 mismatches against a range-walk of '1 unit >= 8 through 22 ... pattern continues'). All five manual examples come out as CMS prescribes: Ex1 24/23 -> 3 units, 2x97112 + 1x97110; Ex2 20/20 -> 3 units split 2+1; Ex3 33/7 -> 2x97110 + 1x97140; Ex4 18/13/10/8 -> 1 each 97110, 97140, 97116, none for 97035; Ex5 7/7/7 -> 1 unit. The 'at least one unit per full 15 minutes' rule holds because whole blocks are assigned first. The gap is the headline comparison: on the shipped example it says the per-code count 'gives 13 units, 3 more than the CMS method allows' (13 - 11 = 2) and 'would overbill by about $48.90' while the visits where per-code exceeds CMS add $77.30; the dollar figure nets Visit C's per-code shortfall against the others, and with a visit mix where the shortfall dominates it prints 'overbill by about -$30.00' next to '1 more than the CMS method allows' (run).
evidence.completeness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 16/16 pass. Every feature in the README and page checked via analyze(): total-time units, allocation to codes, per-code comparison, untimed codes listed and excluded (97014, 97161 in the example), unknown codes warned, repeated codes summed, near-miss flag (Visit E, 35 min, 3 to next), rates with default fallback, CSV export, opt-out local usage counts honouring DNT/GPC (usage.mjs:34). served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin left. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: 16 tests pass and pin the CMS table at its boundaries, the per-code threshold, two allocations and the sum invariant for every pair 0..60. Seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: reversed remainder order (calc.mjs:52) caught, per-code '>= 8' -> '> 8' (calc.mjs:44) caught, near-miss '<= 3' -> '<= 2' (calc.mjs:118) caught; dropping the Math.max floor on per-visit 'over' (calc.mjs:115) survived; deleting 97116 from the timed list (calc.mjs:8) survived (its minutes silently become a warning). 3 of 5 caught. A sixth (floor((m+7)/15) -> round(m/15)) survived but is equivalent for whole minutes, so not counted. None of the five CMS manual examples is a test, and the totals/headline aggregation is untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (133 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, both test files. Pure exported functions, HTML escaped, sensible warnings. Defects: the separator class `[ \t:,=x-]+` swallows a minus sign, so '97110 -5' is read as 5 minutes with no warning (run); 'over' is floored per visit but the dollar difference is not, so the headline mixes two definitions (calc.mjs:115 vs :124); dense one-line HTML building in index.html:129-130.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not advice), placeholder-data note, no-patient-identifiers note and a 'Not decided' section are on index.html and README; page.test asserts them. No-upload claim backed: grep for fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon finds none and page.test asserts it. Formula claims in the README and FAQ match the code (table run above). Weak spots: VENTURE.yaml and the JSON-LD description name speech therapy clinics, but the timed cognitive codes 97129/97130 that OT and SLP bill are not on the list and are dropped; the page's 'overbill by about $X' sentence is not what the code computes (net difference, can be negative). llms.txt's github.io source URL is rewritten at deploy (source-only, not counted).
evidence.fitness: Walked a front-desk biller's job: paste a day's visits, read units by code, see which payer method changes the count, export CSV. The example runs in a second and answers it for PT. An OT or SLP clinic billing 97129/97130 cannot finish: those minutes are excluded with a warning telling the user to 'add it' though the page has no way to add a timed code. PT and OT on the same day must be entered as separate visits (fine, but unstated).
evidence.domain: Against Pub. 100-04 ch. 5 section 20.2 C the method is the CMS method: total timed minutes set the units, whole 15-minute blocks stay with their code, remaining units go to the largest leftover minutes (the manual's Example 3 reasoning), ties to the first listed (the manual allows either). The per-code comparison is the CPT 'substantial portion' count some commercial payers use. Departures: the timed code list omits 97129/97130 (timed 15-minute cognitive-function codes since 2020); MPPR, modifiers and the DRA per-day unit limits in section 20.2 D are stated as not modelled.

defects.what: Headline comparison mixes definitions: 'over' is floored at 0 per visit but the overbill dollars are the net per-code minus CMS revenue across all visits. The shipped example reads '13 units, 3 more than the CMS method allows' (13 - 11 = 2) and 'overbill by about $48.90' when the visits that exceed CMS add $77.30; a mix where per-code falls short prints 'overbill by about -$30.00'.

Timed cognitive-function codes 97129/97130 (OT/SLP, 15-minute units) are not on the timed list, so their minutes are dropped and the visit undercounted; the warning says to 'add it' but the page offers no way to, though the page and VENTURE.yaml target speech and occupational therapy clinics.

Tests miss core changes: dropping the per-visit floor on 'over' and deleting a timed code (97116) both leave 16/16 green; none of the five CMS manual examples is a test, and totals/headline aggregation is untested.
The code/minutes separator class includes '-', so '97110 -5' parses as 5 minutes with no warning.

verdict: A small, honest 8-minute-rule tool whose core is right. Checked against the CMS Claims Processing Manual ch. 5 section 20.2 C itself (downloaded from cms.gov), the unit table matches for every whole minute 0..300 and all five manual examples allocate units to codes as CMS prescribes. Disclaimer, placeholder note, no-PHI note and a 'Not decided' list are on the page, and nothing is uploaded. A therapy billing specialist would object to the headline comparison, which counts per-visit excess units but nets dollars across visits (the example says '3 more' and '$48.90' where the excess visits add $77.30, and another mix prints 'overbill by about -$30.00'), and to the missing timed codes 97129/97130 for the OT and SLP clinics it targets. 16 tests pass; 2 of 5 seeded core mutants survive. Does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (correctness 3, claims 3, median 3). Finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: sum the overbill only over visits with over > 0, add 97129/97130, reject negative minutes, and add the five CMS examples plus a totals test.
